title: german political funk threatens timid recovery 2026 08 28
author: Pierre Briancon
text:
LONDON, Aug 28 (Reuters Breakingviews) - Friedrich Merz has a bad case of Starmeritis: the affliction that leaves European leaders, like the former UK prime minister, unable to stem a tide of public discontent. Merz's position ​could become untenable if his conservative CDU performs poorly in regional elections next month. Nervous MPs may conclude he is not ‌the leader to counter the far-right AfD, which is soaring in the polls.
Merz is the most unpopular German chancellor in 30 years. Only 16% of the respondents are satisfied
, opens new tab
 with him, according to a survey published by ARD Deutschland in May. That’s less than for his predecessor Olaf Scholz at the end of his term, and even lower
, opens new tab
 than ​for former UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer days before he was ousted by his own party.
Merz's unpopularity is striking given the economy ​is moving again after five years of stagnation. Germany's GDP grew by 0.3% in the second quarter of the ⁠year, faster than forecast. The last ifo index showed the highest level
, opens new tab
 of optimism in a year among business leaders. And in spite of geopolitical ​uncertainties, Chinese competition and rising energy prices, export expectations are at their highest
, opens new tab
 since February 2022 - just before the start of the war in Ukraine.
Merz’s coalition ​government with the social democrats of the SPD has also delivered a serious economic plan. It announced last month a programme including tax cuts, pension reforms, and measures to tackle Germany's stifling bureaucracy. But these policies will take time to produce results, while a €500 billion taboo-breaking spending programme to shore up infrastructure is yet to be deployed.
The chancellor ​will test his popularity in real time soon. On September 6th, voters in Saxony-Anhalt will flock to AfD, according to polls showing the far-right ​party polling
, opens new tab
 at around 42% of the vote. That's about 20 percentage points ahead of the CDU and 16 percentage points above the populist party's national average. The question ‌is ⁠whether the AfD will take control of the local parliament with an absolute majority of seats. If it does, economic frustration would be a bigger explanation than the party's main platform plank - its virulent opposition to immigration.
Saxony-Anhalt is the poorest of Germany’s 19 regions. Its GDP per capita
, opens new tab
 last year was 40% below the level of the country’s richest region, Bavaria, and 14% below the German average. Like all regions of former communist Eastern Germany, it trails ​the Western part of the country ​by most metrics. And its ⁠population is aging faster than most other parts of Germany. In a central forecast scenario
, opens new tab
 it would lose 13% of its working age population in the next 10 years, while the number of people above 67 will swell by ​8%.
Politics may overtake Merz before he can point to economic success. A resounding electoral defeat would fuel ​pressure from within his ⁠own party, risk months of political paralysis in Berlin and turmoil in the EU ahead of France's high-risk presidential election next year. CDU politicians should think twice before they follow the UK's path of early leader-ousting.
